mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month moving average in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 3-month moving averages signals a labor market expansion with low unemployment, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 3-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when RSAFS falls for three consecutive months.
